messages:
mike: Heads-up — TailwindPay asked for a dedicated batching config change. Their app is latency-sensitive on short chats but also spikes tokens for receipts parsing. They want higher token budget per GPU and a slightly looser queue limit so fewer rejections.

lara: can you paste their current config + the perf numbers that motivated this?

mike: current (prod-dedicated):
```json
{
  \"token_budget_per_gpu\": 80000,
  \"queue_limit\": 64,
  \"max_batch_tokens\": 2048,
  \"max_wait_ms\": 8,
  \"kernel_policy\": \"auto\"
}
```

mike: tailwind saw p95 token latency regress from 68ms -> 74ms since we flipped kernel selection heuristics two weeks ago. KV cache hit rate also dropped from 81% -> 72% for their workload (many short-turn chats).

sachin: that kernel change was the heuristic that prefers fused kernels for seq_len > 64; could be mis-triggering on mixed sequences. Do we have a flamegraph or profiler?

eva: I pulled a short perf profile yesterday — attaching snippet:
```text
PROFILE SNIP
- serving/runtime dispatch: 40ms
- kernel (fused_attn) peak: 18ms (was 12ms before)
- kv-cache lookup: 6ms (was 3ms)
- batching wait overhead: 3ms
```

mike: thanks. My read: two things to address for TailwindPay request — raise token_budget_per_gpu to reduce early rejections, and add a kernel override to prefer legacy kernel for smallish sequences to avoid the 50% regression we see on their mix. Also tune queue_limit up slightly.

lara: propose a canary config to test on their dedicated pool:
```json
{
  \"token_budget_per_gpu\": 125000,
  \"queue_limit\": 96,
  \"max_batch_tokens\": 4096,
  \"max_wait_ms\": 12,
  \"kernel_policy\": \"prefer_legacy_for_seq_le_128\",
  \"kv_cache_warmup\": true
}
```

sachin: question: token_budget increase will raise memory pressure. For their instance type (A100-80G) 125k budget ~= additional 6GB headroom worst-case. Are they on a 2x card pool or single-card nodes?

mike: tailwind dedicated -> 1 GPU per worker (80G). They agreed to a short maintenance window. ops will monitor OOM.

eva: suggest adding a temporary token-bookkeeping metric so we can observe per-worker budget consumption. e.g., `tailwind.token_budget.used` and `..queued_rejections`.

mike: agreed. Also will enable KV cache warmup for their common prefixes — we have a script to prepopulate the KV store for the last 1k request IDs.

lara: steps to roll canary (short):
1) apply canary config to 2 workers in tailwind prod pool
2) route 5% traffic for 1h, collect p50/p95/p99, kv hit rate, OOM events
3) if p95 improves or at least doesn't regress >2%, scale to 20% for 4h
4) rollback if OOM or p95 regresses >5% or rejections spike

sachin: for kernel selection tweak, can we add a temporary override tag so kernel selection code picks legacy for any request with max_seq <= 128? Minimal code: `if max_seq <= 128 and model in tailwind_models -> kernel = legacy`.

eva: will add a short tracepoint to capture chosen kernel per request. Nice to have: `kernel_choice` field in traces.

mike: I'll draft the rwctl command for ops:
```bash
rwctl dedicated update --customer tailwindpay --batch-config '{"token_budget_per_gpu":125000,"queue_limit":96,"max_batch_tokens":4096,"max_wait_ms":12,"kernel_policy":"prefer_legacy_for_seq_le_128","kv_cache_warmup":true}'
```

mike: also notified @deploy-bot to schedule the canary window at 23:00 UTC tonight.

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance: tailwindpay canary roll (2 workers) at 2026-03-18T23:00:00Z — check runbook: https://internal/runbooks/tailwind-canny. :white_check_mark:

lara: LGTM — sachin, eva, can one of you own monitoring during the canary?

sachin: I can take first 2h watch, will alert if memory > 75% or OOMs.

eva: I'll own tracing and kv metrics. Will forward a short report at +2h.

mike: thanks. After the 6h canary we reconvene and decide to roll to full pool or revert.

mike: one more note — if we see persistent kv hit drop, we may need to tune prefix hashing in the cache to avoid fragmentation; that'll be a follow-up.
